before: A row, column, or table delete tombstoned its rows or cells and recorded no deletion for the paragraphs inside them, so when another replica deleted the same content and undid, the content showed again with text the first replica had deleted. An undo of typing recorded no deletion unless a copy of the typing already showed, so a copy that a concurrent join wrote showed the undone typing. An edit of a paragraph that showed text from a split paragraph whose listing a held-back update carried rewrote that text, and an undo of the edit hid it. An undo of a step that created a node deleted the attributes and namespace bindings the step wrote for it, so a node a peer listed again at the same time, such as a moved table's separator paragraph, lost its paragraph identity.
after: The delete also records the text of every paragraph inside a removed row, cell, or table, as it does for a paragraph it removes. An undo records every character it typed and removes, so concurrent copies stay hidden, and its redo withdraws the record. The operation gate refuses, as waiting, an edit of a paragraph that shows following text from a paragraph a held-back update lists. An undo keeps the attributes and bindings of the nodes its step created, as it keeps their records.
reason: The writer adds ordinary deletion records to the existing docx-text-deletions-v1 map, which released replicas of this format already read and withdraw on redo. The gate is replica-local and writes nothing. Keeping a created node's attributes and bindings writes fewer ordinary map deletions; released readers interpret the retained entries with the same meaning, and an unlisted record shows nowhere. No stored field, identity, conflict rule, or canonical mapping changes, so a mixed room converges. Released replicas keep their released behavior for their own edits until they upgrade.
